Audio of one caption, resolved the way e:
Audio of one caption, resolved the way export and recognition hear it.

2026-10-10 (proofread workspace, user report "按播放聽到完全無關的音訊"):
the proofreading page used to seek ``project.media.path`` with the caption's
*timeline* milliseconds. Edited projects place timeline 0 deep inside a source
(and later clips in other files), so every preview played unrelated speech.

A preview here is never computed with a private conversion. The caption's
stable id is looked up in the live project, its range is expressed in the
project timeline, and the clipped audio graph is compiled by the same
``compile_audio_mix`` that renders the recognition input and exports (which
also binds FLV sources to their continuous content clock). Each request
leaves a diagnostic row with the cue, clips, sources and the final range.

The stdio MCP server (``mcp_stdio``) is a thin translator. Every request
reaches this bridge over a per-user named pipe (QLocalServer, current-user
access only, plus a random key) and runs on the GUI thread against the
project open in Studio:

* read tools answer from the open project (paged, searchable);
* edits are two steps: ``preview_*`` builds a plan bound to the project id,
  its edit revision, the scope and a summary; ``apply_plan`` shows the plan in
  an in-product dialog and only the user's click applies it, through the
  existing undoable commands as one undo step. Nothing a client sends
  ("confirmed": true or otherwise) can skip the dialog. A plan is single-use
  and becomes stale as soon as the project changes;
* exports go to "<project folder>/MCP 匯出" through the normal exporter,
  which never replaces an existing file.

Intra-phrase spacing for conversational:
Intra-phrase spacing for conversational subtitles (2026-09-20 rework).

Separates independent interjections, repeated acknowledgements and whole-phrase
repeats with plain U+0020 spaces, driven by word-level timestamps where
available (audio evidence, not blind text heuristics).

User contract:
- Idempotent: applying twice yields the same string.
- Conservative: never splits legitimate words ("好像還不錯", "這個判斷是對的").
- Trailing interjections stay attached ("蹲一下不虧啊").
- U+0020 only; never full-width, zero-width, or runs of spaces.

Local MCP access: settings, the GUI pipe, the access key and path checks (2026-10-12).

Shared by the running GUI (``mcp_bridge``) and the stdio server process
(``mcp_stdio``). Stdlib only: the stdio process must start fast and must
never print anything except protocol messages on stdout.

* The feature is off by default. Settings live under the additive ``mcp`` key
  of the Studio settings file (``enabled``, ``scope``, ``allow_edits``,
  ``allow_export``).
* While enabled, the GUI listens on a per-user named pipe and writes a random
  key next to the settings; the stdio server reads the key for every request.
  Turning the feature off (or "撤銷授權") stops the pipe and deletes the key,
  so new requests fail at once.

Main / secondary speaker roles in the St:
Main / secondary speaker roles in the Studio timeline (2026-10-12).

``studio_state["speaker_roles"]`` (absent on older projects, which keep one
track per speaker until the user organizes them):

    {"policy": "speaker-roles-v1", "grouped": true, "expanded": false,
     "auto": {"S07": "secondary", ...},   # classification snapshot
     "manual": {"S03": "own"},            # user choices, always win
     "rule": "...", "media_ms": 1440000, "source": "recognition" | "organize"}

The automatic part is a snapshot taken when roles are decided (new
recognition, or the explicit "organize" action). Later edits, splits and
merges never re-run it, so a speaker cannot flip between the group and an own
track while the user works; "重新判斷" runs it again on purpose. A speaker that
appears later (reassigned cues) has no snapshot entry and keeps an own track.

Roles only change the timeline display: cue ownership, speaker identity,
colour, style, visibility, exports and audio stay as they are.

One definition of every customizable key:
One definition of every customizable keyboard shortcut (2026-10-13).

Menus, tooltips, the shortcut settings page, conflict checks and the key
dispatchers all read this registry, so a changed key shows up everywhere.

Scopes decide what may share a key:

* ``studio``        — the subtitle workbench (not while typing in a text box);
* ``studio.review`` — priority review inside the workbench; while review is on
                      these win over ``studio`` keys (a shared key is shown as
                      "稽核時優先", not as an error);
* ``home``          — the recognition home page;
* ``proofread``     — the AI 詞庫校對 page;
* ``app``           — everywhere (interface zoom). Clashes with any scope.

Different pages never conflict. Bindings are stored in PortableText (``Ctrl``
is Command on macOS) under ``shortcuts`` in the Studio settings file; Studio
commands keep their historic ids, other scopes use ``<scope>.<name>``.

Opt-in QA (``TWOBYTEASR_ACCEPTANCE_SCENA:
Opt-in QA (``TWOBYTEASR_ACCEPTANCE_SCENARIO=update-flow``): the real update flow.

Clicks the real "檢查更新" button against a QA feed (``TWOBYTEASR_UPDATE_FEED``,
channel ``TWOBYTEASR_UPDATE_CHANNEL``), records the offer dialog, downloads and
stages the update, and accepts "退出並更新".  ``UPDATE_FLOW_PLAN`` (JSON) can
add a simulated busy recognition worker (the update must refuse) and an
unsaved Studio project (first "Cancel" at the save prompt, then "Save").

After the updater restarted the program, the same scenario sees the expected
new version (``UPDATE_FLOW_EXPECT``), checks once more ("already latest") and
closes normally.  Results: ``<acceptance dir>/update-flow-<version>.json``.

The dialogs run nested event loops, so the audit is a non-blocking state
machine driven by a repeating timer; every click is deferred with
``QTimer.singleShot(0, ...)``.  Ordinary sessions never import this module.

Ordinary-word guards and stutter cleanup:
Ordinary-word guards and stutter cleanup for caption *display* text.

2026-10-10 (proofread workspace, user report): the glossary review treated
every reduplication (剛剛, 再再, 這這, 學學) as a missing proper-noun
association, and a near-sound rule turned the ordinary phrase 學聰明了 into
學蟲鳴了. Reduplication is mostly ordinary language or a stammer, and a
common word that reads naturally in its sentence is not evidence of a
misheard game term.

Stutter cleanup here only *proposes* deletions for the display text. It never
merges across captions or speakers, never touches numbers, interjections,
emphatic repeats or glossary terms, and it separates a spoken repetition
(word timing / independent transcripts agree) from a duplicate that no
recognizer heard (left for data repair, not hidden by cleanup).

資料與評分規則（P0）：

- 一個比較組（comparison group）只能來自**同一來源、同一協議**的一張評測表；
  不同資料集 / 指標 / 硬體 / 歸一化流程的數字絕不合併成一個組。
- 組內相對分：錯誤率類（CER/WER/AAS，越低越好）
  ``score = round(100 * sqrt(組內最佳 / 當前值))``；
  吞吐類（RTFx，越高越好）``score = round(100 * sqrt(當前值 / 組內最佳))``。
  分數是 2ByteASR 的相對指數：100 = 該基準組相對最佳，不是識別正確率。
- “組內最佳”取全表（含未註冊的外部系統，如 Doubao/GPT-4o/閉源模型），
  保證“100 = 同表最佳”語義成立；未註冊系統僅在技術說明裡作參考行。
- 缺失、非法、跨協議記錄不計分；組內只有本模型一行且無外部參照時不顯示分數
  （避免“只有一行資料也拿 100”的誤導）。
- 評分繫結：比較場景 + 基準組 + 參照集合 + 公式版本（SCORE_FORMULA_VERSION）。
  搜尋 / 篩選 / 只看已安裝不改變任何分數。
- 本模組是純資料 + 純函式，無 Qt、無網路；評測快照隨包內建，斷網可用。

Content offsets where cutting the text changes its numeric events.

    2026-10-16 (users: "字幕保真檢查未通過" with AI line breaking off): the
    final check compares ``numeric_event_values`` per cue, and a Chinese
    numeral only counts with its context (第/還剩 before it, 個/把/金幣 after
    it, or standing alone). Cuts that read fine - 一萬｜金幣, 一百多｜把,
    還剩｜一條命 - change what each side counts, so splitters avoid them.

    Offset ``b`` is the cut before the b-th content character, the index the
    line breakers use (``content_exact``). Each cut is judged inside a window
    of ``window`` content characters on both sides: the window edges affect
    "cut" and "not cut" alike, so only the cut itself can make a difference.

Shared by the running GUI (``mcp_bridge``) and the stdio server process
(``mcp_stdio``). Stdlib only: the stdio process must start fast and must
never print anything except protocol messages on stdout.

* The feature is off by default. Settings live under the additive ``mcp`` key
  of the Studio settings file (``enabled``, ``scope``, ``allow_edits``,
  ``allow_export``; 2026-10-17 ``allow_glossary`` for the term libraries,
  which belong to no project and so are not covered by ``scope``).
* While enabled, the GUI listens on a per-user named pipe and writes a random
  key next to the settings; the stdio server reads the key for every request.
  Turning the feature off (or "撤銷授權") stops the pipe and deletes the key,
  so new requests fail at once.

  recognize  record, then the home-release-flow driver (real local recognition)
